title: Obrom (two-hollow log drum)
summary: A long log lies on two crossed supports at dusk. Two hollows are carved in its top and joined by a narrow channel, so the left one speaks low and the right one high.
howToPlay: Four places are lit: Left hollow, Right hollow, Side and End.
Strike the place a closing ring marks.
Two pitches are enough to make a signal or a dance tune.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Two carved hollows give a single log two voices: a signal drum and a dance drum at once.
credits: Tradition: the log slit drum called obrom; patterns written for this game
